<!-- pr-reviewer: 4bdebe33a71eca879d983983c882e64a8e63bccb -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Reviewed as an independent check of the PR head `4bdebe3`, trial-merged with current `main` in a clean worktree. Thank you for the thorough writeup - the measured moves, the cause, and the two pinning tests made this easy to verify.

## What looks good

- The fix is the minimal, correct move: `retract` (deburr.rs:265) is exactly the vertical rapid the path already ended with, hoisted to run before each traverse. A rotationally-symmetric cone leaving its break straight up cuts nothing on the way out - the decision record's reasoning for choosing the rapid over a feed retract checks out.
- The traverse into each run is unchanged, cut moves are untouched, and the path's end is the same as before - so existing comparisons still hold. First run: `at()` starts at the clearance plane, so `retract` is a no-op there, as documented.
- No zero-length move can leak out: `PathBuilder::push` already drops a move whose `to == at` (crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs:273), so the retract-plus-traverse pair stays clean even when the next run starts where the last ended.
- Law check is clean: no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests in the diff; module provenance header intact; new helper documented with the law it states; `deburr.rs` is 316 lines, under the ~400 ceiling; no component declared outside `schema.rs`; nothing touches UI, so the command law is not engaged.
- Process is all present: `Changelog:` line, body ends `Fixes #304`, conventional commit subject, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and the decision file matches the `docs/decisions/README.md` format (`## #304 - <title>`, chosen/why/dropped/cost).
- Honest scoping: you say plainly that the break still reads as a gouge to the post gate (#303) and this PR only removes the part of the refusal that was a real motion fault. Agreed that that split is right.

## Local results (merged with main, Windows 11)

- Trial merge with current `main` (which has moved ~200 files since your base `8f30bee`): clean, no conflicts; `main` never touched `deburr.rs` since your base, so nothing to reconcile.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run`: builds clean.

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-motion --lib | 149 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `deburr` | 8 passed (incl. the new pin) |
| app `deburr_links` (new) | 1 passed |
| app `operations` | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `area_controls` | 13 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 68 passed |
| app `ribbon` | 11 passed |
| app `tool_law` | 4 passed |
| app `probe_op` | 11 passed |

The app totals reproduce your run exactly (225 passed, 6 ignored, counting `deburr_links`).

- Negative control: with only `deburr.rs` reverted to `main` (new tests kept), the motion pin fails with your quoted text verbatim - `rapid 10 leaves cutting depth diagonally: Point3 { x: 40.0, y: 0.0, z: -12.0 } -> Point3 { x: 0.0, y: 20.0, z: 20.0 }`. The test pins the fix, as claimed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (finished, no warnings under `-D warnings`).

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The strict `cur.z < clearance_z` test in `retract` means a run that ends with its tip exactly at the clearance plane (possible only when `top_z == clearance_z`, which `validate` allows) emits no retract and the traverse starts horizontally at clearance - still safe, just noting the one corner where "vertical before every traverse" is vacuous by design.
- `retract`'s comment says "the path's start" as the case where it stands at clearance; it's also vacuous after a run clipped to end at the ceiling in the corner above. A one-word tweak at most.
- Not exercised here, same as you said: the windowed app, Linux, macOS. The change is platform-neutral motion code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
